clue.text: Writer wasted, but not with form of consumption

indicators.note: 'not with' tells you to drop the letter that abbreviates the word with

blocks.note: a nib is the writing point of a pen, standing for the pen itself
to blow money is to waste it, so wasted is blew
W is the standard abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: A writer has squandered everything, yet not on any particular way of using things up.
explanation.walkthrough: W is a standard abbreviation for 'with', so 'not with' removes that single letter rather than a whole word.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking small bites is one way of eating, so a little bite counts as a manner of consuming food.

clue.text: Breach of law during French court case

blocks.note: during something is in it
FR is the abbreviation for French
a legal action is a case brought in court

explanation.surface: A legal violation happened while a French trial was under way.
explanation.definitionFit: An infraction is a violation of a rule or statute, often a minor offence against the law.

clue.text: Vintage director's filthy material

blocks.note: a cru is a wine of a particular vineyard or vintage, as in grand cru
D abbreviates director

explanation.surface: An old film-maker's output is dismissed as smut.
explanation.walkthrough: Vintage reads as an adjective for the director, but it is a wine term.
explanation.definitionFit: Crud is informal for dirt, grime or any disgusting sticky substance.

clue.text: Man nearly detained in Kuwait on vacation

indicators.note: someone detained is held inside, so one piece sits within the other
a place on vacation is emptied, so only its outside letters remain

blocks.note: the first and last letters of Kuwait
nigh is an old word for near or nearly

explanation.surface: A man was almost held prisoner while on holiday in Kuwait.
explanation.walkthrough: NIGH goes inside K...T. Man here is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess each piece is called a man, and the horse-headed piece is one of them.

clue.text: State prohibiting act of Congress?

blocks.note: surface reading: a nation banning legislation passed in Washington
setter's reading: congress is an old word for sexual intercourse, so the state is one of sexual abstinence

explanation.surface: Some country outlaws a piece of American legislation.
explanation.walkthrough: Congress capitalised suggests the US legislature, but its old sense is sexual union; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: Celibacy is the condition of abstaining from sex, which rules out any sexual coupling.

clue.text: Straight and too respectable for gaming area

blocks.note: someone above a thing considers it beneath them
games like chess are played on a board

explanation.surface: Someone honest and too decent to sit down at the gambling table.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean honest and open, with nothing hidden or underhand in the dealings.

clue.text: Taking two lots of vaccines periodically would be futile

indicators.note: taking two at a time, and then periodically, means pairs of letters are kept and skipped by turns
periodically means at regular intervals along the word, keeping some letters and skipping others

blocks.note: keep the first pair of letters, skip the next pair, keep the next pair, skip the last

explanation.surface: Getting a double dose of jabs at intervals would achieve nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The pattern is unusual: letters are taken in pairs, VA and IN, with CC and ES discarded.
explanation.definitionFit: Vain effort is useless effort that produces no result, the same as pointless or fruitless.

clue.text: Save record held by court introduced by former partner

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped within it
introduced by means preceded by, so the partner comes at the front

blocks.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
CT is the abbreviation for court
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Keeping a disc that a court is holding, brought in by an ex.
explanation.definitionFit: Save as a preposition means apart from or but, as in 'all save one'.

clue.text: Part of sovereign or ancestral state displaying little enlightenment

indicators.note: part of tells you the answer is a stretch of the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the whole middle word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A royal or inherited realm that is culturally backward.
explanation.walkthrough: State reads as a country in the surface, but it is a condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking knowledge or education is a condition of being unenlightened, which is what the word names.

clue.text: Heard what's used to fiddle objects of desire

indicators.note: heard means we go by what the ear picks up, not the spelling

blocks.note: a violin, or fiddle, is played with a bow

explanation.surface: Things used for cheating, as overheard, turn out to be things people crave.
explanation.walkthrough: Fiddle suggests cheating, but it is the violin.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaux are boyfriends or admirers, the men a person longs for romantically.

clue.text: Sleeping men apparently showing little interest

indicators.note: those sleeping are lying in bed, so the men are placed inside it

blocks.note: people who are sleeping are in bed
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Men nodding off evidently weren't engaged by what was going on.
explanation.walkthrough: Sleeping both supplies BED and puts the men in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone bored is weary and uninterested, so they display scant attention.

clue.text: Vice and anger could become a source of resentment

indicators.note: could become hints that the letters may turn into something new when rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wickedness and rage may breed bitterness.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' joins the two fodder words and is not part of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A grievance is a complaint or cause for bitter feeling over being wronged.

clue.text: Spell "preference" without a 'p'

indicators.note: without means remove, and the letter to go is named outright

blocks.note: a penchant is a liking or preference

explanation.surface: An instruction on how to write the word preference, minus a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: Spell looks like a spelling command, but it is the verb meaning bewitch.
explanation.definitionFit: To spell someone, in the sense of casting a spell, is to bewitch or charm them.

clue.text: Entitled lives getting written about

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

blocks.note: a book written by someone is authored by them
lives in the sense of exists

explanation.surface: A privileged life story being penned.
explanation.walkthrough: Lives is the verb meaning exists, not the plural of life, despite the life-story feel of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Being entitled to do something means having official permission or sanction for it.

clue.text: Compass taking in two points of the surrounding area

indicators.note: taking in means admitting inside, so one piece is held within the other

blocks.note: ambit means scope or range, a sense of compass
E and N, east and north, are two compass points

explanation.surface: A navigator's compass reading two bearings across the nearby terrain.
explanation.walkthrough: Compass is not the instrument but its other sense of range; the points are directions.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambient describes conditions in the immediate environment, such as noise or temperature around you.

clue.text: Inflexible military cuts almost destroy Guards

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
to guard something is to surround it protectively

blocks.note: to end something is to finish it off
trenches are ditches cut by an army

explanation.surface: Rigid defence cuts nearly wreck the Guards regiments.
explanation.walkthrough: Guards looks like soldiers, but it is the containment verb; cuts is a noun for ditches.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrenched position or attitude is firmly established and hard to shift or change.

clue.text: Section in novel by Hardy: it's a celebration of life

indicators.note: novel means new, so the following letters are made into something new
in places the section inside the other letters

blocks.note: the letters of these words are the fodder
a part is a section

explanation.surface: A passage from a Thomas Hardy novel is said to celebrate life.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram gives BIRTHDAYY and PART slips in before the final Y. Novel looks like a book by Hardy, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A party held on the anniversary of someone's birth marks and celebrates their being alive.

clue.text: All but the beginning of absurdist broadcast is upsetting

indicators.note: all but the beginning means everything except the opening letter
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Most of a surreal programme on air is upsetting viewers.
explanation.definitionFit: Disturbs means troubles or unsettles someone, which is to say it upsets them.

clue.text: Windy hollow around middle of ground

indicators.note: around means one piece encircles the other
middle of means keep only the central letters

blocks.note: a sinus is a hollow cavity, as in the skull
the two central letters of ground

explanation.surface: A breezy dip in the middle of a field.
explanation.walkthrough: OU goes inside SIN...US. Windy means winding, as a road, not breezy.
explanation.definitionFit: A windy road twists and turns, so it is full of curves, which is what sinuous describes.

clue.text: Newspaper employee receives a fine

indicators.note: receiving something means taking it in, so one piece is placed inside

blocks.note: a sub is a subeditor on a newspaper
a, as in 'ten pounds a head', means per

explanation.surface: A journalist gets a penalty payment.
explanation.walkthrough: A fine looks like a penalty, but fine is the adjective meaning excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine can mean of high quality, and superb is an emphatic word for excellent.

clue.text: Where one might deliver speech

blocks.note: first meaning: the house and street a parcel is sent to
second meaning: a formal talk to an audience

explanation.surface: The place where a speaker gives an oration.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one idea about delivering a speech; split it into two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both the location written on post and a formal oration given to listeners.

clue.text: What provides introduction to aristocratic place?

definitions.text: What provides introduction to aristocratic place?

indicators.note: an introduction is what comes first, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of aristocratic
a venue is a place where something happens

explanation.surface: Asking what leads the way up to a stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a tree-lined drive is the approach to a country house.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a broad tree-lined drive leading up to a grand house, its formal approach.

clue.text: Force opening of safety lock

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the first letter of safety
a lock of hair is a tress

explanation.surface: Breaking open a safety catch by brute strength.
explanation.walkthrough: Lock is hair, not a fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: In physics and engineering, stress is the force applied per unit area of a material.

clue.text: Quietly play hackneyed phrase?

blocks.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for soft
play as in freedom of movement, slack

explanation.surface: A tired saying muttered softly in a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Play is not a drama but room to move.
explanation.definitionFit: A platitude is a trite remark used so often it has lost any force or freshness.

clue.text: American tune recalled part of opera?

indicators.note: recalled suggests calling back, so the tune runs in the opposite direction

blocks.note: A abbreviates American
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A US melody remembered as a piece from an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song for a single voice within an opera or oratorio.

clue.text: Part of core curriculum to come up time and again

definitions.text: to come up time and again

indicators.note: part of signals a run of letters inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters span the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A subject in the essential syllabus that keeps reappearing.
explanation.definitionFit: To recur is to happen repeatedly, coming back again and again.

clue.text: What one did in cowboy competition mainly

definitions.text: What one did in cowboy competition mainly

indicators.note: mainly means most but not all, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: a rodeo is a contest of cowboy skills

explanation.surface: Asking what a cowboy chiefly did at a riding contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: at a rodeo the competitors mostly ride.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding broncos and bulls is the main event at such a contest, and the past tense fits 'did'.

clue.text: Upgrade level in auditorium

indicators.note: an auditorium is where an audience listens, so we go by the sound

blocks.note: to level a building is to raze it to the ground

explanation.surface: Improving the seating tier in a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: Level is a verb meaning flatten, and its sound gives the opposite of flattening.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to lift it to a higher grade or level, to promote it.

clue.text: Order to restrict jumping with no restraint

blocks.note: to bound is to leap
an instruction to cut down on something tells you to do it less

explanation.surface: A command to stop leaping about, given freely.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as a command, 'Bound less!', telling someone to jump less.
explanation.definitionFit: Something boundless has no limits or borders, so nothing holds it in check.
